newsitem.title: UK: LME copper starts slow, aluminium shoots higher.
newsitem.headline: LME copper starts slow, aluminium shoots higher.

text.p: The base metals started mixed on Tuesday morning after Monday's holidays in the U.K. and U.S., with business in flagship copper scrappy and prices easier.
Aluminium, however, zipped up from last week's lows past $1,650 resistance on a bout of speculative buying. It was last trading at $1,658, a gain of $25 from Friday's close.
One trader said a big long had been overhanging the market but seemed to have unwound the position.
That in turn sparked fresh speculative buying against the backdrop of a reasonable chart close on Friday and an LME stock decline of 1,825 tonnes.
The aluminium cash to three months contango narrowed to around $7 from $11 on Friday.
The opposite speculative scenario was said to have pulled the rug out from under nickel, which sank nearly $100 to a low of $7,450 before recovering slightly on shortcovering.
It was last at $7,490/$7,510, versus $7,530 on Friday.
"It was all one way traffic, with the buying in aluminium coming from one area and the selling in nickel coming from another area," a trader said.

Fundamental news appeared to have little effect on the metal, although the market noted news that the union representing 4,700 Inco Ltd employees had requested the assitance of a provincial mediator in contract talks with the giant Canadian nickel producer. The contract expires on May 31.
Other recent news included expectations that the European Comission would recommend that new euro coins contain only limited amounts of nickel.
Copper prices edged lower in slow trade and traders said they expected it to consolidate because the market was technically overbought, with the 14-day RSI at around 78.
Prices were indicated at $2,506/$2,509, compared to $2,520 on Friday. Initial support was at $2,500, but the $2,480/90 level is also important technically.
An LME stock draw of just 650 tonnes provided little upward impetus, but cash/threes backwardation was steady at $80/$85.
Zinc was buoyant and near recent 4-1/2 year highs at $1,366, up $3 from Friday.
A stock draw of 2,775 tonnes was helpful, but the metal was looking increasingly overbought and analysts said it was overdue for a correction. Support was seen at $1,350 and then $1,325.
The other metals were dull and little changed from last week's finish.Tin was up $30 at $5,740, and lead was stagnant at $632/$635, versus $633.
